methods.label: Complete the square from a known side
methods.explanation:
Two consecutive midpoints are already known, so they give a fixed side of the square. Let \(E,F,G,H\) be the midpoints of \(AB,BC,CD,DA\), respectively. Then
\[
E=(2,5),\qquad F=(3,2).
\]
Moving from \(E\) to \(F\) changes the coordinates by \((1,-3)\). The next side of a square is perpendicular and equally long, so its coordinate change is a quarter-turn of this one. A quarter-turn interchanges the horizontal and vertical changes and reverses one sign. Thus the change from \(F\) to \(G\) is either \((3,1)\) or \((-3,-1)\), giving
\[
G=(6,3)\quad\text{or}\quad G=(0,1).
\]
Because \(G\) is the midpoint of \(C=(5,3)\) and \(D\), doubling its coordinates and subtracting those of \(C\) gives
\[
D=(7,3)\quad\text{or}\quad D=(-5,-1).
\]
The first-quadrant condition requires both coordinates to be positive, so \(D=(7,3)\).

For this point, \(H=(5,6)\), which is the required fourth square vertex: the change from \(E\) to \(H\) is \((3,1)\), the same as from \(F\) to \(G\). Hence this candidate satisfies the full square condition. The requested sum is \(\boxed{7+3=10}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
